TLINE.TDLINE: &TITLE&
Funktionstrennungsanalyse
&PURPOSE&
Dieser Analysereport zeigt SOD-Konflikte von Benutzern/Rollen gemäß dem
ihnen zugeordneten Zugriff an. Sie können bei der Analyse die Konflikte
in Benutzern oder Rollen nach verschiedenen Auswahloptionen anzeigen.
Nach der Analyse wird die SOD-Scan-Tabelle mit den entsprechenden
Konflikten des in den Auswahlkrit. enthaltenen Benutzers aktualisiert.
&INTEGRATION&
&PREREQUISITES&
Das Berechtigungsobjekt Y&SW_RPOUG prüft den Benutzerzugriff
auf die Benutzergruppe des analysierten Benutzers.
&FEATURES&
Ausführungsmodus:
Nach Ben.-ID(s): Geben Sie spezifische Benutzer-IDs ein, zu denen die
Analyse erfolgen soll
Systemübergr. (RFC): Soll die SOD-Analyse über mehrere Systeme erfolgen,
können Sie die RFC-Destinationen angeben, für die Sie die Analyse
durchführen möchten. Dies ist sinnvoll, wenn mehrere Produktivsysteme/
-umgebungen mit abweichenden Benutzerzugriffen in den beiden
Systemen vorliegen.
<ZH>Beispiel 1:</>
SAP R/3 für Rechnungswesen, Fertigung und HR
SAP CRM für Kundenstamm und Transaktionen
<ZH>Beispiel 2:</>
2 verschied. R/3-Produktivsysteme; eines für 1 Geschäftseinheit/Sparte,
das andere für alle sonstigen Geschäftseinheiten/Sparten.
Nur Benutzer im lokalen System analysieren: Wird zusammen mit der Option
"Systemübergr. (RFC)" verwendet, um nur jene Benutzer zu analysieren,
die im lokalen System vorliegen, in dem der Report ausgeführt wird.
<ZH>Beispiel:</>
,,,,Report wird im R/3-System ausgeführt. Der Benutzer JOHND existiert
im R/3- und CRM-System, ,,,,der Benutzer MARYJ aber nur im CRM-System.
JOHND wird analysiert, MARYJ wird nicht analysiert.
Nur Remote-Systeme analysieren: Bei aktivierter Option werden alle
benutzerbezogenen Infos des lokalen Sys. ignoriert. Dies ist hilfreich
bei SOD-Analysen aus einem Zentralsystem, das das SOD-Regelwerk enthält,
aber keine produktiven Benutzerdaten.
Nach Ben.-Gruppe(n): Soll die Analyse nach BenGruppe erfolgen, markieren
Sie den Auswahlknopf und geben Sie spezif. BenGruppen in das Feld ein.
Nach Pers.-Bereich(en): Soll die Analyse nach dem Personalbereich des
Benutzers erfolgen, markieren Sie den Auswahlknopf und geben Sie
spezifische Personalbereiche in das Feld ein.
N. Rollen: Soll die Analyse nach bestimmten Rollen erfolgen, markieren
Sie den Auswahlknopf und geben Sie diese Rollen in das Feld ein.
Rollen geändrt zwschn: Soll die Analyse für bestimmte Rollen erfolgen,
die vor kurzem angelegt oder geändert wurden, geben Sie das Start- und
Enddatum ein. SW führt die Analyse für alle Rollen aus, die zwischen
diesen Zeitpunkten angelegt oder geändert wurden.
Dies ist sinnvoll, wenn Rollen geändert werden und Sie prüfen möchten,
ob SOD-Konflikte in den zuvor angelegten/geänderten Rollen vorliegen.
Rlln anzgn (Drucktaste): Diese Drucktaste dient zum Anzeigen der Rollen
gemäß den unter "Rollen geändrt zwschn" angegebenen Zeitpunkten vor dem
Ausführen der Analyse.
Nur in Remote-Systemen: Wird zusammen mit der Option "Remote-System
(RFC)" verwendet, um nur jene Rollen in den Remote-Sys. zu analysieren,
die über die RFC-Destination(en) angegeben sind. Die Rollen werden nicht
im lokalen System analysiert, in dem der Report ausgeführt wird.
Simulation:
Simulrn d. Hinzf. v.Rlln: Hiermit können Sie das Hinzufügen von Rollen
zu Benutzern simulieren. Die Funktion simuliert eine Situation, bei der
der Benutzer neue Rollen besitzt, mit denen dann SOD-Prüfungen erfolgen,
ohne dass Änderungen an der Benutzer-ID vorgenommen werden müssen.
RFC-Destinatnen für Rolle: Befinden sich die zu simulierenden Rollen in
einem anderen System/Mand., geben Sie den Namen der RFC-Destination ein,
in der die Rolle vorliegt. SW ruft alle Rollen aus der Remote-Lokation
Ausführen der Analyse.
Ausgabeeinschränkungen:
Übersicht SOD-Konfl.: Ist dieser Auswahlknopf markiert, zeigt SW nur die
Kopfdaten des Konflikts an (z.B. Benutzer-ID, Name, Konflikt,
Beschreibung usw.); es werden keine Details angezeigt. Die Ausgabe ist
aufrissfähig, d.h. alle Details lassen sich durch Auswahl der
entsprechenden Konflikt-ID einblenden. Der Dokumentation können Sie die
Bedeutung von Spalten, Zellen, Sortierreihenfolge usw. entnehmen.
Dies ist sinnvoll, wenn Sie sich lediglich die Konflikt-IDs zusammen mit
einer kurzen Zusammenfassung der Analyseergebnisse (z.B. durchschnittl.
Anzahl SODs pro Benutzer, Anzahl Benutzer usw.) anzeigen lassen möchten.
Konflikte markieren: Beim Übersichtsmodus haben Sie auch die
Möglichkeit, Zellen verschiedenfarbig nach ihrer Sensitivität zu
markieren: Hoch - Rot, Mittel - Rosa, Niedrig - Blassgelb.
SOD-Konfliktdetails: Bei markiertem Auswahlknopf zeigt SW alle Details
des jeweiligen SOD-Konflikts zu jedem Benutzer an. Die Details umfassen:
Benutzer-ID, RFC-Destination, Konflikt, Funktion, Berechtigungen,
Profile, Rollen, Berechtigungswerte usw.

&TITLE&
Segregation of Duties analysis
&PURPOSE&
This analysis report will display SOD conflicts that users/roles have,
based on the access that they are assigned. You can run the analysis to
display conflict in users or Roles, by various selection options.
After the execution of this analysis, the SOD scan table is updated with
appropriate conflicts for each user included in your selection criteria.
&INTEGRATION&
&PREREQUISITES&
Authorizaiton object Y&SW_RPOUG is used to check for user's access
against the user group of the analyzed user.
&FEATURES&
Execution Mode:
By User ID(s): Enter specific user IDs for which you want to run the
analysis
Cross-System (RFC): If you would like to run the SOD analysis across
multiple systems, you can list the RFC destinations for which you would
like to run the analysis for. This is useful if there are multiple
production systems/environments and users have different access in both
systems.
<ZH>Example 1:</>
R/3 for accounting, manufacturing and HR
SAP CRM for customer master and transactions
<ZH>Example 2:</>
Two different R/3 production systems; one for one business unit/division
, another for all other business units/divisions.
Only Analyze Users that Exist in Local System: Used in conjunction with
the Cross System (RFC) option above to only analyze users that exist in
the local system where the report is being executed.
<ZH>Example:</>
,,,,Report is being executed from the R/3 system. User JOHND exists in
both the R/3 and CRM system ,,,,while user MARYJ exists in only the CRM
system. JOHND would be analyzed while MARYJ would not
Only Analyze Remote Systems: By enabling this option all user-related
information of the local system would be ignored. This is helpful if SOD
analyses are executed from a central system, which holds the SOD rule
set but no production user data.
By User Group(s): If you would like to run the analysis by user group,
select the radio button and fill this field with specific User Group(s).
By Personnel Area(s): If you would like to run the analysis by user's
personnel area, select the radio button and fill this field with
specific Personnel Area(s).
By Role(s): If you would like to run the analysis for specific roles,
select the radio button and fill this field with those specific role(s).
Roles Changed Between: If you would like to run the analysis for
specific roles that were recently created/changed, enter the start and
end dates. SW will run the analysis for all roles that were either
created or changed between those dates.
This is useful when roles are changed and you want to check whether
there were any SOD conflicts in the recently created or changed roles.
Show Roles (push button): You can use this button to display the roles,
based on the dates specified in "Roles Changed Between," before running
the analysis.
Only on Remote System(s): Used in conjunction with the Remote System
(RFC) option above to only analyze roles in the remote system(s)
specified by the RFC destination(s). The role(s) will not be analyzed
in the local system where the report is being executed.
Simulation:
Simulate by Adding Roles: You can use this to simulate adding roles to
users. Using this feature, you can simulate a situation where the user
would have new roles and run SOD checks with new roles, all without
actually having to make any changes to the user ID.
RFC Destination for role: If the role(s) you want to simulate is on a
different system/client, enter the name of RFC destination where the
roles exist. SW will fetch all roles from the remote location and run
the analysis.
Output Restrictions:
SOD Conflict Summary: With this radio button selected, SW will only
display the header information of the conflict (e.g. User ID, Name,
Conflict, Description, etc.), no details will be displayed. The output
has drill-down capability; so all details can be displayed by selecting
the appropriate conflict ID. See documentation for the meanings of
columns, cells, sort order, etc.
This is useful when you would like to see just the conflict IDs along
with a brief summary on the analysis results (e.g. average SODs per
users, total users, etc.).
Highlight Conflicts: With the summary mode, you also have the option to
highlight the cells in different colors based on their sensitivity. High
- Red, Medium - Pink, Low- Pale Yellow.
SOD conflict details: With this radio button selected, SW will display
all details of each SOD conflict for every user. Details will include:
User ID, RFC destination, Conflict, Function, Authorizations, Profiles,
Roles, Authorization Values, etc.
This is useful when you would like to see all the conflict details for
all users upfront. Commonly used when diagnosing and identifying the
root cause of the SOD conflicts in users and roles. You will need this
information to resolve conflicts for users/roles.
The output has drill-down capability, so further details can be
displayed by selecting the appropriate cell in the grid. Information
like Object definition, Field definition, Possible values, Activity Text
, Transaction Text, and much more are available by double-clicking. See
documentation for the meanings of columns, cells, sort order, etc.
SOD conflict details tree: With this radio button selected, the SE
report will display all details of each SOD conflict for every user in a
hierarchy tree format. The hierarchy is: User Group, User, Sensitivity
, Conflict ID, Function ID, System/Client, and Authorization Object.
Then, Authorization name, Field, From/To Values, Role, Role Description
, and Profile.
Show Comp. Role(s): Fill this check-box if you would like to see the
composite roles (in the detailed report output) that are providing the
user with the single roles that appear in the detailed output.
Dynamically Enhance Matrix: Fill this check-box if you would like to
see the SOD conflicts that result from custom programs. Note: This will
increase processing time.
Highlight Dynamically Enhanced Conflicts: This is grayed out until the
'Dynamically Enhance Matrix' option is checked.
Show only these conflicts: With this you can restrict the scope of the
SOD analysis to specific conflicts that interest you. SW will only run
the analysis for the conflicts that you specify here.
Sensitivity: With this you can restrict the scope of the SOD analysis
to specific sensitivity levels that interest you. SW will only run the
analysis for the conflicts that have the sensitivity levels that you
specify here.
SOD Version: Enter the SOD matrix version to use for the analysis.
Valid and Dialog Users only: Fill this check-box if you would like to
run this analysis for all non-locked, non-expired, dialog users only.
If this check-box is left empty, the analysis will include all users
including, for example, background and locked users.
Show Mitigating Controls: By default, the program ignores users that
already are assigned mitigating controls for the conflicts that they
have. If you would like to show these conflicts on the report, fill this
checkbox to show the users that are mitigated for the conflicts that
they have. This option also allows maintenance of the mitigation
assignments at the Summary level report.
Show Users w/o Conflicts: Fill this check-box if you would like to
display a message, in the output, stating there are no conflicts for
users that do not have any conflicts, but were included in your
selection criteria.
Update Scan table: Fill this checkbox if you would like to update the
SCAN table with appropriate conflicts for each user included in your
selection criteria. This SCAN table is populated to be used in the Graph
reporting.
Include ER Roles: This checkbox will show up in the selection if the
Emergency Repair application is found on that system. This will be
unchecked by default. You can fill this checkbox if you would like to
analyze the ER roles in the SOD conflict Analysis (as if they were
assigned normally).
Org. level check: Fill this check-box if you.d like to do a conflict
analysis including the organization level objects in the rules.
Org Level: This is grayed out until the 'Org. level check' option is
checked. With this you can restrict the scope of the organizational
level analysis by a specific org area.
Conflict Origin: Checkboxes for Local, Remote, or Cross system to limit
the report conflicts that are resulting from which system.
Background processing:
Since processing mass amount of data would most likely cause your
session to Time-Out and create a Short Dump, SW provides you an
intuitive functionality to schedule a background job for these large
analyses.
Schedule Background Job: Hit this button to start the background job
wizard, which will guide you, step-by-step, in scheduling the background
job.
You can modify and adjust all fields in the background job wizard, but
do not change program name and variant.
Note: This button will not appear if the user lacks background job
administrative privileges (authorization object S_BTCH_ADM).
View Jobs (SM37): This button will take you to transaction SM37, in
which you can monitor your jobs. You will need access to transaction
SM37.
Note on Dynamic Enhancements:
Security Weaver SOD reports have the capability to enhance the SOD
matrix by adding transactions codes identified by the following methods:
Call Transactions
Parameter Transactions
Variant Transactions
Leave to Transactions
Submit statements
By dynamically enhance the SOD matrix, there is no need to identify and
manually insert all transactions that are calling (or using) the same
transactions that are part of the SOD matrix already. This enhancement
includes SAP and all custom transactions. To activate this option check
the .Include enhanced ruleset. option.
By default the scope of this report is to perform this analysis on all Y
and Z transactions. However, the scope can be customized by executing
program /psyng/sw_074 via transaction SE38.
Note: Program /psyng/sw_078 can be used to add additional scope to this
report when configuration parameter SW_ENH_LOCAL_FILT is set to 'Y'.
However, this is only needed in a very limited set of circumstances.

This analysis report will display SOD conflicts that users/roles have,
based on the access that they are assigned. You can run the analysis to
display conflict in users or Roles, by various selection options.
After the execution of this analysis, the SOD scan table is updated with
appropriate conflicts for each user included in your selection criteria.
&INTEGRATION&
&PREREQUISITES&
Authorizaiton object Y&SW_RPOUG is used to check for user's access
against the user group of the analyzed user.
&FEATURES&
Execution Mode:
By User ID(s): Enter specific user IDs for which you want to run the
analysis
Cross-System (RFC): If you would like to run the SOD analysis across
multiple systems, you can list the RFC destinations for which you would
like to run the analysis for. This is useful if there are multiple
production systems/environments and users have different access in both
systems.
<ZH>Example 1:</>
R/3 for accounting, manufacturing and HR
SAP CRM for customer master and transactions
<ZH>Example 2:</>
Two different R/3 production systems; one for one business unit/division
, another for all other business units/divisions.
Only Analyze Users that Exist in Local System: Used in conjunction with
the Cross System (RFC) option above to only analyze users that exist in
the local system where the report is being executed.
<ZH>Example:</>
,,,,Report is being executed from the R/3 system. User JOHND exists in
both the R/3 and CRM system ,,,,while user MARYJ exists in only the CRM
system. JOHND would be analyzed while MARYJ would not
Only Analyze Remote Systems: By enabling this option all user-related
information of the local system would be ignored. This is helpful if SOD
analyses are executed from a central system, which holds the SOD rule
set but no production user data.
By User Group(s): If you would like to run the analysis by user group,
select the radio button and fill this field with specific User Group(s).
By Personnel Area(s): If you would like to run the analysis by user's
personnel area, select the radio button and fill this field with
specific Personnel Area(s).
By Role(s): If you would like to run the analysis for specific roles,
select the radio button and fill this field with those specific role(s).
Roles Changed Between: If you would like to run the analysis for
specific roles that were recently created/changed, enter the start and
end dates. SW will run the analysis for all roles that were either
created or changed between those dates.
This is useful when roles are changed and you want to check whether
there were any SOD conflicts in the recently created or changed roles.
Show Roles (push button): You can use this button to display the roles,
based on the dates specified in "Roles Changed Between," before running
the analysis.
Only on Remote System(s): Used in conjunction with the Remote System
(RFC) option above to only analyze roles in the remote system(s)
specified by the RFC destination(s). The role(s) will not be analyzed
in the local system where the report is being executed.
Simulation:
Simulate by Adding Roles: You can use this to simulate adding roles to
users. Using this feature, you can simulate a situation where the user
would have new roles and run SOD checks with new roles, all without
actually having to make any changes to the user ID.
RFC Destination for role: If the role(s) you want to simulate is on a
different system/client, enter the name of RFC destination where the
roles exist. SW will fetch all roles from the remote location and run
the analysis.
Output Restrictions:
SOD Conflict Summary: With this radio button selected, SW will only
display the header information of the conflict (e.g. User ID, Name,
Conflict, Description, etc.), no details will be displayed. The output
has drill-down capability; so all details can be displayed by selecting
the appropriate conflict ID. See documentation for the meanings of
columns, cells, sort order, etc.
This is useful when you would like to see just the conflict IDs along
with a brief summary on the analysis results (e.g. average SODs per
users, total users, etc.).
Highlight Conflicts: With the summary mode, you also have the option to
highlight the cells in different colors based on their sensitivity. High
- Red, Medium - Pink, Low- Pale Yellow.
SOD conflict details: With this radio button selected, SW will display
all details of each SOD conflict for every user. Details will include:
User ID, RFC destination, Conflict, Function, Authorizations, Profiles,
Roles, Authorization Values, etc.
This is useful when you would like to see all the conflict details for
all users upfront. Commonly used when diagnosing and identifying the
root cause of the SOD conflicts in users and roles. You will need this
information to resolve conflicts for users/roles.
The output has drill-down capability, so further details can be
displayed by selecting the appropriate cell in the grid. Information
like Object definition, Field definition, Possible values, Activity Text
, Transaction Text, and much more are available by double-clicking. See
documentation for the meanings of columns, cells, sort order, etc.
SOD conflict details tree: With this radio button selected, the SE
report will display all details of each SOD conflict for every user in a
hierarchy tree format. The hierarchy is: User Group, User, Sensitivity
, Conflict ID, Function ID, System/Client, and Authorization Object.
Then, Authorization name, Field, From/To Values, Role, Role Description
, and Profile.
Show Comp. Role(s): Fill this check-box if you would like to see the
composite roles (in the detailed report output) that are providing the
user with the single roles that appear in the detailed output.
Dynamically Enhance Matrix: Fill this check-box if you would like to
see the SOD conflicts that result from custom programs. Note: This will
increase processing time.
Highlight Dynamically Enhanced Conflicts: This is grayed out until the
'Dynamically Enhance Matrix' option is checked.
Show only these conflicts: With this you can restrict the scope of the
SOD analysis to specific conflicts that interest you. SW will only run
the analysis for the conflicts that you specify here.
Sensitivity: With this you can restrict the scope of the SOD analysis
to specific sensitivity levels that interest you. SW will only run the
analysis for the conflicts that have the sensitivity levels that you
specify here.
SOD Version: Enter the SOD matrix version to use for the analysis.
Valid and Dialog Users only: Fill this check-box if you would like to
run this analysis for all non-locked, non-expired, dialog users only.
If this check-box is left empty, the analysis will include all users
including, for example, background and locked users.
Show Mitigating Controls: By default, the program ignores users that
already are assigned mitigating controls for the conflicts that they
have. If you would like to show these conflicts on the report, fill this
checkbox to show the users that are mitigated for the conflicts that
they have. This option also allows maintenance of the mitigation
assignments at the Summary level report.
Show Users w/o Conflicts: Fill this check-box if you would like to
display a message, in the output, stating there are no conflicts for
users that do not have any conflicts, but were included in your
selection criteria.
Update Scan table: Fill this checkbox if you would like to update the
SCAN table with appropriate conflicts for each user included in your
selection criteria. This SCAN table is populated to be used in the Graph
reporting.
Include ER Roles: This checkbox will show up in the selection if the
Emergency Repair application is found on that system. This will be
unchecked by default. You can fill this checkbox if you would like to
analyze the ER roles in the SOD conflict Analysis (as if they were
assigned normally).
Org. level check: Fill this check-box if you.d like to do a conflict
analysis including the organization level objects in the rules.
Org Level: This is grayed out until the 'Org. level check' option is
checked. With this you can restrict the scope of the organizational
level analysis by a specific org area.
Conflict Origin: Checkboxes for Local, Remote, or Cross system to limit
the report conflicts that are resulting from which system.
Background processing:
Since processing mass amount of data would most likely cause your
session to Time-Out and create a Short Dump, SW provides you an
intuitive functionality to schedule a background job for these large
analyses.
Schedule Background Job: Hit this button to start the background job
wizard, which will guide you, step-by-step, in scheduling the background
job.
You can modify and adjust all fields in the background job wizard, but
do not change program name and variant.
Note: This button will not appear if the user lacks background job
administrative privileges (authorization object S_BTCH_ADM).
View Jobs (SM37): This button will take you to transaction SM37, in
which you can monitor your jobs. You will need access to transaction
SM37.
Note on Dynamic Enhancements:
Security Weaver SOD reports have the capability to enhance the SOD
matrix by adding transactions codes identified by the following methods:
Call Transactions
Parameter Transactions
Variant Transactions
Leave to Transactions
Submit statements
By dynamically enhance the SOD matrix, there is no need to identify and
manually insert all transactions that are calling (or using) the same
transactions that are part of the SOD matrix already. This enhancement
includes SAP and all custom transactions. To activate this option check
the .Include enhanced ruleset. option.
By default the scope of this report is to perform this analysis on all Y
and Z transactions. However, the scope can be customized by executing
program /psyng/sw_074 via transaction SE38.
Note: Program /psyng/sw_078 can be used to add additional scope to this
report when configuration parameter SW_ENH_LOCAL_FILT is set to 'Y'.
However, this is only needed in a very limited set of circumstances.

intuitive functionality to schedule a background job for these large
analyses.

wizard, which will guide you, step-by-step, in scheduling the background
job.

do not change program name and variant.

View Jobs (SM37): This button will take you to transaction SM37, in
which you can monitor your jobs. You will need access to transaction
SM37.
Note on Dynamic Enhancements:
Security Weaver SOD reports have the capability to enhance the SOD
matrix by adding transactions codes identified by the following methods:
Call Transactions
Parameter Transactions
Variant Transactions
Leave to Transactions
Submit statements
By dynamically enhance the SOD matrix, there is no need to identify and
manually insert all transactions that are calling (or using) the same
transactions that are part of the SOD matrix already. This enhancement
includes SAP and all custom transactions. To activate this option check
the .Include enhanced ruleset. option.
By default the scope of this report is to perform this analysis on all Y
and Z transactions. However, the scope can be customized by executing
program /psyng/sw_074 via transaction SE38.
Note: Program /psyng/sw_078 can be used to add additional scope to this
report when configuration parameter SW_ENH_LOCAL_FILT is set to 'Y'.
However, this is only needed in a very limited set of circumstances.
